name: Gradient
tagline: Accessible color scales from one brand color, where the step number tells you the contrast. Light and dark mode, OKLCH, export for Tailwind and CSS.
seoTitle: Gradient – accessible OKLCH color scales with dark mode for Tailwind and CSS
description:
Gradient turns one brand color into eleven steps from 50 to 950, for light and dark mode, plus a grey tinted with your hue. Most palette generators space lightness evenly, so contrast depends on the hue: blue-600 passes on white, yellow-600 often does not. Gradient solves every step for a fixed contrast instead. Step 500 always reaches 3:1, step 600 4.5:1 and step 800 7:1 against the page, in dark mode against black, for every color you start from.

Colors are computed in OKLCH and brought into sRGB by lowering chroma only, so the contrast stays where it was solved. Every step comes with a readable text color for buttons and badges. Export the palette as a Tailwind CSS v4 theme, a Tailwind v3 config, CSS custom properties, W3C design tokens or JSON, from code or with one CLI command. No dependencies, MIT-licensed.

faq.q: Does Gradient keep my exact brand color?
faq.a: By default the closest step gets your hue and chroma, with lightness adjusted to the contrast of that step. Pass --pin to keep the exact color; the contrast check then tells you if that breaks a promise.

faq.q: Why are the colors in OKLCH?
faq.a: OKLCH is perceptually even: the same lightness looks equally bright in every hue, and chroma changes do not shift the hue. All browsers since 2023 support it. Use the hex export for older ones.

faq.q: Does a passing contrast check make my site accessible?
faq.a: It covers the contrast criteria of WCAG 2.2 (1.4.3, 1.4.6 and 1.4.11). It cannot tell whether information depends on color alone or how the colors are used. For checks of the whole site, see Surjection.
No. Gradient is MIT-licensed and complete. It is also the color foundation of the upcoming UI library Lattice.

faq.q: Can people with a color vision deficiency tell my colors apart?
faq.a: Run gradient --check or checkDistinguishable(). It simulates protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia and lists the pairs that look alike at step 600. For those, add an icon or a label: color alone is never enough for status messages.

gradient check and checkPair() show the APCA value (Lc) next to the WCAG 2 ratio. Pass and fail follow WCAG 2.2, because that is the standard the European Accessibility Act refers to; APCA is part of the WCAG 3 draft and shown for information.

faq.q: How do I use Gradient with shadcn/ui?
faq.a: Run npx @sweberdev/gradient "#e30613" --format shadcn --out app/globals.css and replace the theme section of your globals.css. The file has the variables for :root and .dark and the @theme inline mapping for Tailwind v4. Text on background reaches 7:1, buttons and badges 4.5:1, form field borders 3:1.

faq.q: Can I use Gradient for colors I already have?
faq.a: Yes. gradient audit app/globals.css reads custom properties that end in a step number (--color-brand-600, --blue-500), from :root, a dark class or media query, or light-dark(), checks the pairs the step numbers promise and suggests a color that passes. It exits with 1 on a failing pair, so it works in CI.

faq.q: Why does a gradient between blue and yellow look grey in CSS?
faq.a: CSS blends in sRGB by default, and the average of two opposite colors there is a grey. gradient blend and createBlend() blend lightness, colorfulness and hue instead, so the middle stays as colorful as the ends. Current browsers can do the same with linear-gradient(in oklch, …); createBlend returns both strings.

faq.q: Can Gradient read a color from my logo?
faq.a: extractColors() takes the pixels of an image (RGBA, for example ImageData.data from a canvas) and returns the dominant colors with their share; pickBrand() chooses the one that works as a brand color. There is no command line version because the command line cannot decode images, and nothing is uploaded: the demo reads the image in your browser.

faq.q: How do I keep generated color files up to date in CI?
faq.a: Put your colors in gradient.config.json (gradient init writes a starter file) and run gradient build --verify in CI. It writes nothing and exits with 1 when a file is missing or differs, a contrast promise fails or an audited stylesheet fails. The GitHub Action Weber-Development/gradient@v0 does the same on pull requests and comments the result.

faq.q: Will my generated files change when I update Gradient?
faq.a: Not within a major version: for the same input and options the generated colors and files stay byte for byte the same, unless a release fixes a broken contrast promise, which the changelog names. The tests snapshot every output format to enforce this. Run gradient build --verify in CI to see whether committed files differ.
